title: Data Engineering Trends: Spark and Machine Learning Integration
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- Apache Spark and machine learning topics are seeing increased interest.
- Engineers are exploring text embeddings and vector search at scale.
- Data migration challenges remain a frequent pain point.
- Modern stacks involving dbt and Snowflake continue to be standard.

Interest in Apache Spark and machine learning is rising as data engineers look to integrate advanced analytics into their pipelines. Discussions centered on generating text embeddings at scale and implementing vector search for multimodal data. Practitioners are actively seeking guidance on how to leverage Spark for these AI-driven tasks, reflecting a broader shift toward building production-ready systems that go beyond traditional ETL.

Core data engineering workflows remain focused on migration and transformation. Data migration continues to be a significant source of frustration, with engineers sharing "horror stories" and seeking advice on managing complex database transitions. Meanwhile, dbt remains a staple for transformation, with ongoing debates regarding the practical use of ephemeral materialization and the integration of AI agents to streamline analytics delivery.

Career development and platform architecture also featured prominently this week. Professionals are navigating transitions between software engineering and data roles, often dealing with imposter syndrome or evaluating new job offers. On the technical side, architects are debating the implementation of One Big Table (OBT) within medallion architectures and optimizing large-scale data loads into Apache Iceberg.
